paragraphs: Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.

In Bava Metzia 85a it is told that Rabbi happened upon the locale of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon (after his death) and asked whether a son remained of that righteous man. They told him: He has a son, but he does not conduct himself properly. He had him brought before him, invested him with the title Rabbi, and handed him over to Rabbi Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya, his mother's brother. When he grew up he sat in Rabbi's academy, and when Rabbi heard his voice he said: This voice resembles the voice of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. They told him: He is his son.

And when he died they wished to bring him into his father's cave but could not. A heavenly voice went out and said: Not because this one is greater than that one, but his father suffered the distress of the cave (when he fled with his father Rabbi Shimon), and this one (his son) did not suffer the distress of the cave. And in Tanchuma, Vayera-Lekh, the incident is transmitted mistakenly.

And in Tosefta Kiddushin chapter 1 we find Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Elazar saying in the name of Rabban Gamliel: Anyone who has a trade in hand is like a fenced vineyard. Hyman considers it likely that this is Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, and that Rabban Gamliel is the son of Rabbi.

notes.text: Asmekheih be-Rabbi gives him the title Rabbi, rather than merely making him Rabbi’s student. Hyman calls his uncle Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya; the named Davidson text reads ben Isi. Hyman’s Tanchuma criticism and tentative Tosefta identification remain his own.
The supplied Tanchuma locator וירא-לך remains unresolved. The named Torat Emet Vayera text returned no match for the cave account in the reviewer’s bounded search.

The complete inspected Bava Metzia 85a episode gives the title Rabbi, the uncle Shimon ben Isi, the voice comparison and the cave refusal. Hyman gives Yose rather than Isi. Tosefta Kiddushin chapter 1 directly has Yose בר״א reporting Rabban Gamliel and the fenced-vineyard saying; the proposed full identity and identification of Gamliel as Rabbi’s son remain Hyman’s tentative conclusions. The supplied Tanchuma locator remains unresolved.
